newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Nov 8.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Nov 8.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Mark Taylor put on record yesterday in several interviews that Australia will not have to call on David Boon to help the nation's cricket chances. The comments came after Boon said he might resurrect his career if the troublesome number three batting postion could not be filled. Page 20.

The Victoria Racing Club committee will have the last say early next week over whether or not jockey Darren Beadman will ride Melbourne Cup winner Saintly in the Japan Cup, after stewards outed him yesterday at Flemington till the end of the month. Page 2.

Holden's sponsorship of the women's Australian Open golf tournament is in doubt for next year, with an announcement due at the end of the tournament's last day. The event was revived by Holden three years ago at Royal Adelaide. Page 18.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Poor form on tour may have ended winger David Campese's career after he was dropped from the Wallaby side for Saturday's Test against Scotland. Campese wants to regain his number one ranking on the team by the end of the year and prove critics wrong that he is finished with rugby union. Page 42.

The newly established Rugby Union Players' Association has taken legal action to ensure the Australian Rugby Union meets commitments made in the famed "Ferrier document", a document signed last year by rugby union chief Ian Ferrier. Page 41.

Marconi soccer club is considering whether to enter a rugby league team in the Metropolitan Cup next year. The move is inspired by an agreement to share grounds between the Sydney Olympic soccer club and Canterbury rugby league team. Page 41.
THE AGE

Darren Beadman incurred the wrath of the stewards at Flemington yesterday, getting himself suspended for careless riding. He is now at the mercy of the VRC committee as to whether or not he will be allowed to ride Saintly in the Japan Cup. Page C8.

Jan Stephenson and Karrie Webb are continuing a feud that begun in America in May, with neither of the two golfers saying more than "good shot" to the other in yesterday's lead up game to the women's Australian Open. Page C8.

Former Test cricket captain Bill Lawry has called for the selection of Victorian Matthew Elliott, saying that Australia can no longer afford the luxury of Michael Slater's extravagant opening stroke play. Page C6.
HERALD SUN

Champion jockey Darren Beadman will appeal against the severity of his 21-meeting suspension so that he can ride Saintly in the Japan Cup. is suspension came after he caused interference on 7-2 favourite Dashing Eagle in yesterday's VRC Oaks. Page 104.

The Carlton Soccer Club was registered as a company yesterday and will start with a working capital of around A$2 million. The initial membership drive hopes to raise at least A$500,000 for the club. Page 102.

Lee Freedman has had a career high success by winning yesterday's Group 2 Linlithgow Stakes with one of his favourite horses, Mahogany. The win comes after 74 Group 1 wins and the taking of every major race on the Australian calendar by Freedman. Page 10.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Mark Ella, one of the all time greats of Australian rugby union, has launched a stinging attack against Australian coach Greg Smith for his decision to drop winger David Campese for tomorrow's game against Scotland. Page 110.

Gai Waterhouse was accused by an industrial court yesterday of underpaying two employees more than A$16,000 for overtime they worked. The court said the bonus paid to strappers was not an adequate compensation for hours they had worked. Page 109.

Mouawad is set to have a great horse racing career after he won in the A$50,000 Moet & Chandon Stakes (1400m) at Flemington yesterday, winning the race by two and three quarter horse lengths ahead of Suburbia and Maximal. Page 108.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
